summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Embryogeny: Zygote -> Proembryo -> Globular -> Heart-shaped -> Mature embryo. Monocot grass embryo: 1 shield cotyledon (Scutellum), Coleoptile (plumule sheath), Coleorhiza (radicle sheath), Epiblast. Perisperm (persistent 2n nucellus in Black Pepper, Beet). Albuminous (Castor, Maize) vs Exalbuminous (Pea, Bean) seeds.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DICOT vs MONOCOT EMBRYO ANATOMY
                    
      DICOT EMBRYO (Capsella)                   MONOCOT EMBRYO (Poaceae)
      ├── Embryonal Axis (Tigellum)             ├── Single Cotyledon (Scutellum)
      ├── 2 Lateral Cotyledons                  ├── Coleoptile (Plumule Sheath)
      ├── Epicotyl ──► Plumule                  ├── Coleorhiza (Radicle Sheath)
      └── Hypocotyl ──► Radicle & Root Cap      └── Epiblast (Remnant 2nd Cotyledon)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 8.1 Dicotyledonous vs. Monocotyledonous Embryogeny

```
                       EMBRYO DEVELOPMENTAL STAGES
                       
   Zygote (2n) ──► Proembryo ──► Globular Embryo ──► Heart-Shaped Embryo ──► Mature Embryo
```

### 8.2 Post-Fertilization Structural Transformations

```
                         FLORAL TO SEED/FRUIT MAPPING
                         
   Ovary Wall               ──────────► Pericarp (Exo, Meso, Endocarp)
   Ovule                    ──────────► Seed
   Outer & Inner Integuments──────────► Seed Coat (Outer Testa + Inner Tegmen)
   Nucellus                 ──────────► Degenerates OR persists as Perisperm
   Synergids & Antipodals   ──────────► Degenerate
```

- **Perispermic Seeds**: Persistent, thin, functional remnant of the **diploid Nucellus ($2n$)** in mature seeds (e.g., *Black Pepper, Beet, Nymphaea*). *(Note: Perisperm is $2n$, whereas Endosperm is $3n$)*.
- **Albuminous (Endospermic) Seeds**: Retains triploid endosperm tissue as a storage organ at seed maturity (e.g., *Castor, Sunflower, Wheat, Maize, Barley*).
- **Exalbuminous (Non-Endospermic) Seeds**: Endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo prior to seed maturation; food is stored in cotyledons (e.g., *Pea, Gram, Bean, Groundnut*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Suspensor & Haustorial Function
conceptBreakdown.title: Suspensor & Haustorial Function
conceptBreakdown.content: During early embryogeny, the basal cell divides to form a 6-10 celled Suspensor whose top swollen vesicular cell (Haustorium) pushes the developing proembryo deep into the nutritive endosperm tissue.

conceptBreakdown.heading: The Orchid Exalbuminous Exception
conceptBreakdown.title: The Orchid Exalbuminous Exception
conceptBreakdown.content: While the vast majority of monocots have endospermic (albuminous) seeds, Orchids are a notable evolutionary exception, producing millions of microscopic dust-like exalbuminous seeds without endosperm.
